newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: C&W rules out renewed alliance talk with BT.
newsitem.headline: C&W rules out renewed alliance talk with BT.

text.p: The chief executive of British telecommunications giant Cable and Wireless (C&W) on Monday poured cold water on reviving negotiations for an alliance with with British Telecommunications Plc following the latter's merger with U.S. firm MCI Communications Corp.
"The coals on that fire are cold," Richard Brown said when asked if failed merger talks between BT and C&W six months ago would be renewed.

"The announcement of BT with MCI and our announcement recently of the formation of Cable and Wireless Communications should be strong messages that we are more competitors than we are partners," Brown said.
"We have looked at the possibility of merging the two companies but in the end it did not make sense. We are very pleased with that decision and we are moving ahead with Cable and Wireless," he said.

Brown, who was in Singapore to open C&W's new office, said his company was not surprised at BT's merger nor was it "frightened by it". BT and MCI have announced plans for a $20 billion merger that would create the world's second-largest telecommunications group based on market capitalisation.

"It was clear BT had to leave the home market to be global... C&W is already a global company, with 70 percent of our revenue outside home country, and we are prepared to sink our roots deeper and be more focused on major markets we are in," Brown said.

According to Richard Goswell, C&W's Southeast Asia and Pacific chief executive, the company was looking at opportunities in Singapore after the government pushed forward the deregulation of telecommunications to 2000 from 2007.

"We would be looking very closely with our existing partners whether this (MobileOne) is an appropriate vehicle to take us forward into this new venture," Goswell said, referring to the company's plans to bid for a wire-line licence in Singapore.
C&W and HK Telecom are partners in the MobileOne consortium that is building Singapore's second cellular communications network.

Goswell said there were no immediate plans to list MobileOne and added that its cellular network project was on schedule: "We should be providing services at the WTO conference on a trial basis." The WTO (World Trade Organisation) conference will be held in Singapore from December 9 to 13.
Company officials declined to indicate investment sums for the fixed wire-line service in the island-state. Brown said C&W had to select its partners first.

Goswell dimissed concerns over Singapore's small population of about three million. "The future of telecommunications is a combination of fixed services, mobile services, entertainment services and information services. Those are the platforms that will meet customers' future needs," he said.
He added that market penetration for wire-line services, unlike the cellular market, cannot be measured based on market size but rather in minutes and information on the network.
Brown dismissed analysts' fears that intense competition and mega-mergers in the telecommunications market would leave only a handful of survivors.

"I don't think the world is well served by five or six telecom companies. There will be many and there will be rich expertise in various niche markets and capabilities and this is good. No one shoe fits all feet," he said.
